Reflection Intensity The example below demonstrates how the reflection intensity controls the reflectivity of the material. Note that this intensity acts as a white filter for the base color. A material with higher reflection intensity reflects more light, so it looks white and blurry. FABRIC MATERIAL TYPE Materiel Type Properties Reflection intensity increases the amount of reflection, and roughness spreads the reflected light. Roughness Roughness controls the sharpness of reflections. Lower values allows light to be reflected in a small area and larger values allows light to be reflected in the whole object area. The amount of roughness can be changed with the Intensity slider, or a custom roughness map may be imported. FABRIC MATERIAL TYPE Normal Maps and Roughness The middle and right image have the same parameters except for the normal map. Nevertheless, the right image looks a bit more rough. The normal map makes the surface of the object bumpy (=rough), so the highlights are reduced. Placing a normal map is similar to increasing roughness. CLO3D.COM l SUPPORT.CLO3D.COM
PDF_Summary: Step-by-Step Instructions: 1. To accurately digitize fabrics with the CLO Fabric Kit, open Emulator Mode. 2. Follow the instructions in the video link provided to digitize fabrics using the Fabric Kit. Definitions: 1. Stretch: Refers to how much the fabric stretches. The lower the number, the more elastic it becomes. Most fabrics have a stretch value of 0~66. 2. Bending: Refers to the fabric stiffness. Bending_10 indicates a lower stiffness, while Bending_70 indicates a higher stiffness. 3. Buckling Ratio: Expresses the shape of a fabric's creases. A higher ratio indicates a more pronounced crease. 4. Density: Refers to the fabric's weight in grams per square millimeters. 5. Silhouette: Refers to the overall shape and outline of a garment. Warranties: 1. If the Grainline is modified for the Texture rotation, the Physical Properties of the garment will be changed as well. 2. Applying Fabric files measured with the actual Fabric and CLO Fabric Kit gives the most realistic silhouette. 3. If there is no actual Fabric, use the most similar Fabric from the Library. 4. Apply Normal Maps to express uneven Textures for a more realistic appearance. 5. Ensure that grids are avoided on repeat and color when applying Textures. 6. Set the DPI of the edited Texture to the same DPI as the original scan to maintain consistency. 7. Note that the silhouette of the garment will change when rotating the Grainline, as it changes the direction of the Texture and Fabric's Physical Properties. 8. Set the appropriate Material Type for the Fabric to achieve the desired appearance. 9. Reflection intensity increases the amount of reflection, while roughness controls the sharpness of reflections. 10. Placing a normal map on the fabric can make the surface appear more rough.
